title: Francis and the Sultan (1219)
hookLine: in the middle of a crusade, Francis crosses the lines to meet Sultan al-Kamil, and is received with courtesy

cards: A crusader army is camped outside Damietta, in Egypt, and the war is going on all around it. Into the camp comes a barefoot friar from Assisi, with a companion, Brother Illuminato. He asks to cross over to the other side.
In the later telling, he's warned he's walking to his death. He goes anyway. Out between the armies, he's seized by the Sultan's soldiers.
Instead of being killed, he's brought before the Sultan himself, al-Malik al-Kamil, ruler of Egypt. An enemy preacher, in the middle of a war, standing before the man he's at war with.

teach.h: A BISHOP'S LETTER FROM THE CAMP.
teach.b: The earliest witness is a bishop in the crusader camp, Jacques de Vitry, who wrote about it in a letter soon after.

In paraphrase: Francis went to the Sultan and preached to him for some days, and the Sultan listened to him closely. Then the Sultan had him escorted back to the camp safely, with respect, and asked him to pray for him.

That's the core. Later biographers add more. Bonaventure tells that Francis offered to walk through fire to show the truth of his faith, that the Sultan declined, and that he offered Francis gifts, which Francis refused.

teach.h: RECEIVED WITH COURTESY, SENT BACK SAFE.
teach.b: But the oldest letter is enough: a friar crossed the lines, spoke of his faith, and was received with courtesy and sent home alive. Notice both sides of that meeting. Francis went without a sword.
And a Muslim ruler, in the middle of a war, listened to an enemy's preacher and protected him. Afterward, Francis wrote guidance for friars who wanted to live among Muslims.

In paraphrase: they should not start arguments or disputes, but be subject to every human creature for God's sake, and say plainly that they are Christians; and only when they see that it pleases God, preach.

teach.h: FIRST SAY, PEACE BE TO THIS HOUSE.
teach.b: It echoes what Jesus told his followers when he sent them out, in the King James words: "into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house." First, peace.
Today some Christians and Muslims tell this story together, as a meeting that went better than the war around it.

how: Franciscans and other Christians sometimes recall this meeting at interfaith gatherings with Muslims, and some Franciscan communities live and work in Muslim-majority countries.

games.q: you're the Sultan al-Kamil. in the middle of a war, your soldiers bring you an enemy friar who's come to preach. what do you do?

games.why: the earliest account, a letter from Jacques de Vitry, says the Sultan listened to him for some days, then had him escorted back safely and asked him to pray for him.

practice: Bring to mind someone on the other side of a line from you, in politics, faith, a family quarrel or a rival team, and picture crossing over the way Francis did: not to win, just to be there.

What would courtesy look like with them: hearing them out to the end, a real greeting, a kind word about something they love? If you pray, pray for them by name; if you don't, wish them well, silently, by name.

wordCard.voice: Al-Kamil. The Muslim Sultan who received the unarmed friar Francis of Assisi with courtesy, and sent him back safe.
